regions.shortDescription: A diagram of three stacked horizontal planes labeled Layer (top), Layer (middle), and Layer (bottom). A black dot marked "start here" sits on the top layer; a blue line traces a path from it to another node, then a dashed blue vertical line drops through the middle layer—where two blue hops are shown among gray nodes—down to the bottom layer, ending at a blue node. An orange dot labeled "query" and a green dot labeled "nearest neighbor" sit near the bottom-left of the lowest layer.
regions.plainLanguage: Three stacked flat layers show a search path: it starts at the top, hops across each layer following the closest node, and ends near an orange query dot and a green nearest-neighbor dot at the bottom.

regions.shortDescription: A four-step numbered list: 1 (black) Start at the entry point on the top layer. 2 (blue) Greedily hop to whichever neighbor is closest to the query. 3 (blue) When no neighbor is closer, drop down one layer and repeat. 4 (green) On layer 0, widen to a small candidate beam (efSearch) and return the best k.
regions.plainLanguage: Four numbered steps describe the search: start at the top, greedily hop to the nearest neighbor, drop a layer when stuck, and at the bottom layer use a wider beam to return the best results.

regions.shortDescription: A light blue bordered box with text: "Coarse layers cover distance; layer 0 does the fine positioning. Only ~dozens of nodes are visited out of millions."
regions.plainLanguage: A highlighted note explains that upper layers quickly cover large distances, while the bottom layer fine-tunes the result, visiting only about dozens of nodes out of millions.
